entries.headline: War Watch relays Seahawk emergency-code report
entries.summary: War Watch Intel relayed a report credited to @reagan0965 that a US Navy MH-60R Seahawk helicopter transmitted emergency transponder code 7700 over the Red Sea near Yanbu, Saudi Arabia. The visible post does not establish the emergency's cause or outcome.

entries.headline: Reconnaissance and transport activity with elevated radio traffic
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported US Air Force reconnaissance and transport aircraft activity across multiple regions and elevated coded radio traffic worldwide. The post does not identify individual flights or explain the broadcasts.

entries.headline: Airborne US transports and three reported radio broadcasts
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported transport aircraft and a surveillance aircraft airborne over the continental United States. It said three coded radio broadcasts had been heard that day, with the latest at 21:50 Zulu.

entries.headline: War Watch relays AFP report of explosions in Saudi capital
entries.summary: War Watch Intel posted an AFP-attributed report that two loud explosions were heard in the Saudi capital. The post does not establish their cause or any casualties.

entries.headline: Three US transports, bomber and command aircraft reported airborne
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported three large US Air Force transport aircraft and a bomber airborne over the United States, alongside surveillance and nuclear command jets. It also reported two coded US Air Force radio broadcasts earlier that day.

entries.headline: War Watch relays Russian laboratory quarantine report
entries.summary: War Watch Intel relayed an Insider Paper report that a Russian laboratory worker's death prompted fears of plague exposure and the quarantine of nearly 200 people. The post credited @reagan0965 without giving a location or independent confirmation of the reported exposure.

entries.headline: Four US cargo jets and nuclear command aircraft reported airborne
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported multiple US Air Force transport and surveillance aircraft airborne over the United States, including four large cargo jets and a nuclear command aircraft. The post did not identify callsigns or specific missions.

entries.headline: War Watch relays suspicious-note report on AJET 4180
entries.summary: War Watch Intel relayed a Faytuks report that a note alleging explosive material had been found aboard AJET 4180, a passenger flight from Ankara to Şanlıurfa. The post did not confirm that explosives were present or describe the flight's subsequent outcome.

entries.headline: US transports, surveillance aircraft and nuclear command jet reported
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported multiple US Air Force transport aircraft over the United States, alongside surveillance aircraft and a nuclear command jet. It described activity as elevated; the visible text did not identify flight missions or give the complete period for its radio-broadcast observation.

entries.headline: Five transports over US and intelligence aircraft sightings reported
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported five US Air Force transport aircraft airborne over the United States, plus surveillance and nuclear command aircraft sightings that day. The post did not identify their callsigns or specific missions.

entries.headline: Five US cargo aircraft and radar jet airborne reported
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported five US Air Force cargo aircraft airborne over the continental United States, along with an airborne radar aircraft and multiple intelligence aircraft sighted that day. The post did not identify callsigns or specific missions.

entries.headline: Four US transports and radar surveillance aircraft reported
entries.summary: War Watch Intel reported four US military transport aircraft and a radar surveillance aircraft airborne over the United States. It also described surveillance aircraft monitoring from domestic bases, without naming the bases, aircraft identities or specific missions.

skyglass.caption: Military aircraft movement reports.

entries.headline: Boeing 737 CNV5406 airborne alert at Lentini
entries.summary: SkyGlass posted an OFF Ground alert for a Boeing 737 with callsign CNV5406 at Lentini, Italy, describing it as US-registered military aircraft. Its destination, passengers and operational purpose are not established by the alert.

entries.headline: P-8 BFLO41 on-ground alert at Burton
entries.summary: SkyGlass posted an ON Ground alert for a P-8 with callsign BFLO41 at Burton, Australia, describing it as Australian-registered military aircraft. The alert does not confirm a mission or the reason for its ground status.

entries.headline: P-8 airborne alert at Al Sajaah
entries.summary: SkyGlass posted an OFF Ground alert for a US military P-8 at Al Sajaah, United Arab Emirates. The callsign appeared as @@@@@@@@; the alert does not establish a destination or operational purpose.

entries.headline: P-8 on-ground alert at Hickam Field
entries.summary: SkyGlass posted an ON Ground alert for a US-registered Boeing P-8 Poseidon at Hickam Field, Hawaii. The callsign was shown as NA; the alert does not establish a mission or deployment purpose.

entries.headline: SkyGlass shares MQ-9B disaster-relief communications demonstration report
entries.summary: SkyGlass shared a Soldier Systems Daily report that GA-ASI and SoftBank had demonstrated a communications system on the MQ-9B aimed at supporting disaster relief connectivity. The post did not give the demonstration's date or confirm use in an actual disaster response.

entries.headline: SkyGlass shares autonomous drone wingman first-flight report
entries.summary: SkyGlass shared a Breaking Defense report about Northrop Grumman's self-funded autonomous drone wingman completing its first flight, identifying the aircraft as YFQ-48A. The post did not provide the flight's date or independent confirmation.

entries.headline: E-6 airborne alert near Suisun
entries.summary: SkyGlass issued an OFF Ground alert for a US military E-6 near Suisun, California. No callsign was supplied, and the post did not confirm a destination or specific mission.

entries.headline: B-52 airborne alert near Midwest City
entries.summary: SkyGlass issued an OFF Ground alert for a US military B-52 near Midwest City, Oklahoma. The callsign field showed 00000000; the post did not confirm the aircraft's identity, destination or specific mission.

entries.headline: P-8 airborne alert near Mundgod
entries.summary: SkyGlass issued an OFF Ground alert for an Indian-registered military P-8 near Mundgod, India. No callsign was supplied, and the post did not confirm a destination or specific mission.

entries.headline: DEPOT11 E-2 airborne alert near Coronado
entries.summary: SkyGlass issued an OFF Ground alert for DEPOT11 near Coronado, United States, describing the aircraft as a US Navy E-2 Hawkeye. The post did not confirm a destination, deployment or specific mission.

entries.headline: NATO02 AWACS ground alert at Albacete
entries.summary: SkyGlass issued an ON Ground alert for NATO02 at Albacete, Spain, describing it as a Luxembourg-registered E-3 AWACS aircraft. The post did not confirm a specific mission or the reason for its ground status.

entries.headline: P-8 airborne alert at Port Hueneme
entries.summary: SkyGlass issued an OFF Ground alert for a US military P-8 at Port Hueneme, United States. No callsign was supplied, and the post did not confirm a destination or specific mission.
